The 24-hour day and 360-day year remain the working canon, and no worldbuilding note advances Gloin's story. ## Inherently good, morally grey and inherently evil magic — creator canon (21 November 2026) Fundamental distinction: Magical forces in Eryndor do not all begin morally neutral. Some varieties of magic are intrinsically benevolent/good, some are morally grey, indifferent, ambiguous or mixed, and others are intrinsically malevolent/evil. This is a characteristic of the magic itself, separate from a practitioner's motives, affiliations, species or self-description. A kind practitioner cannot make an intrinsically evil force innocuous simply by willing good intentions; a cruel practitioner can attempt to exploit fundamentally good magic without changing its essential nature. Good magic need not guarantee good outcomes, and evil magic need not produce the same result on every occasion. No invented universal taxonomy: Which named disciplines, moons, deities or effects occupy these categories has not yet been individually classified. Do not automatically declare all healing good, all shadows evil, or any entire intelligent people inherently good or evil; classification attaches to particular magical forces and their demonstrable nature, not to whole societies. A grey domain is not automatically morally harmless. The moons are actual sources of lunar magic, the planet independently generates Natural Magic, and the peoples know the moons are sources while not knowing how, why or exactly which moon produces which magic. The gods of magic and prayer traditions can be benevolent, morally complex or dangerous without replacing the moons as the source of lunar magic. Some lunar powers are negligible, some immense, and praying to a misunderstood moon can have serious consequences. Continuity: Do not predetermine which moon hides the Veiled Inland Sea, reveal any secret lunar identity to Gloin, invent divine bargains or choose the player's action. This is creator-level cosmology only; the game remains paused at Autumn Day 22, Year 3847 of the Era of Crowns, Fifth Age, \~11:25 AM. ## Canon correction — moons are actual magic sources, known fact; individual workings unknown (21 November 2026) Creator's explicit correction, overriding any earlier ambiguous 'moon as mere focus' or 'gods as independent source' language: Eryndor's natural satellites are real sources of lunar magic. The people of Eryndor know as a general fact that the moons are sources of magic. They broadly do not know how or why moons have magical power, or which particular moon produces, governs or bestows which magical discipline or effect. Scholarly traditions, shrines, astrologers, mages and temples may propose competing identifications; unverified assignments remain claims, not certified facts. This is a limitation on common and scholarly in-world knowledge, not a denial that particular moons have real qualities. Coexisting exceptional source: Eryndor itself independently generates Natural Magic (the World's Breath), as the creator established earlier. Thus the normal cosmic model has two known actual sources of magic: moons for lunar magical forces, and the planet for intrinsic Natural Magic. Neither source cancels or replaces the other. Do not redefine the moons as only symbolic astronomical markers or move their intrinsic magical supply to separately invented gods. Religious interpretation: The 'gods of magic' are the powerful sacred authorities and forces through which societies conceptualize, worship, address and sometimes experience lunar magic. Genuine divine powers may govern or interact with that magic, but are not thereby established as an independent generator replacing the moons. Exact gods, their relationship to moons, and whether a specific moon answers a given prayer remain undecided. Worship can be widespread, differentiated, consequential and dangerous; some moons appear negligible while others are immensely potent. The known moon-to-discipline mapping is not settled, and no character acquires it automatically. Approximately 221–255 moons (working midpoint 238); their full magical roster stays open. Gloin's paused campaign is unchanged. ## The Gods of Magic — metaphysical clarification (creator decision, 21 November 2026) Established setting premise: The 'gods' in the widespread lunar worship traditions are real divine or godlike powers that govern and influence magical forces, rather than merely invented explanations for astronomical bodies. Worship of these magical powers—often through associated moons, observances, offerings and prayers—is a central religious dimension of Eryndor. Divine governance and lunar magical resonance can be potent, faint or effectively inactive; some moons or cult traditions accomplish little or nothing, while others are capable of extraordinary wonders. Gods may be benevolent, indifferent, inscrutable or dark. A prayer to an appropriate magical power can be answered with something astonishing; one directed toward the wrong or dangerous power may invite ruin. None of this guarantees answered prayers, easy magical mastery, or a fixed good-versus-evil outcome for every god. Separate cosmic foundations: The planet itself creates Natural Magic / the World's Breath independently. Gods govern, influence, channel, limit, shape or otherwise exercise authority over magical powers; this does not automatically mean they created Eryndor's intrinsic magical energy. The moons themselves are literal sources of lunar magic, and inhabitants know that without knowing how, why or which one controls which power. Orbital relationships alter influence, but do not assume one separate god per moon, that a moon literally is the god, or that all 221–255 moons must be equally active. Whether gods rule several moons, compete over forces, reside within moons, act through them, or have other relationships is still open. Religion and epistemic distinction: Gods-of-magic as a class are a creator-established world fact. Their specific identities, roster, jurisdictions, deeds, doctrines, motives, manifestations, degree of personhood, public proof and individual affiliations are not yet known. Believers can sincerely disagree, misidentify patrons, maintain corrupt or false cults, and report wonders without understanding their source. Diverse peoples still maintain different traditions, eras, prayers and religious institutions. Preserve mundane social and political religions alongside moon-linked worship; do not create a universal uniform church or define a one-to-one pantheon before the creator does. Campaign boundary: No particular god, divine intervention, cursed moon, pact, prayer or blessing is retroactively added to Gloin Hammerfeld's experience; the exact paused scene is unchanged. ## The moons are actual sources of lunar magic — explicit creator correction (21 November 2026) Directly established canon: Eryndor's natural satellites are genuine sources of lunar magic, not merely signs, conduits or symbols of some separate divine magic generated elsewhere. People throughout Eryndor know as a general fact that magic comes from the moons, although they do not understand how lunar magic arises, why it works, or which specific moon causes or governs which magical effect. They can observe magical influence and pray toward celestial bodies without having an exhaustive verified moon-to-discipline mapping. Some moons may be extraordinarily effective, some negligible or effectively inert; 221–255 moons do not imply 221–255 equally strong or individually understood powers. Crucial independent exception: The planet Eryndor itself produces Natural Magic / World's Breath independently. The creator explicitly established both sources; do not misstate lunar magic as the source of all magic or redefine Natural Magic as moon-derived. The divine powers or 'gods of magic' govern or are involved in the lunar magical forces and form the basis of widespread moon-directed religion, but how they relate ontologically to the moons' production of magic is unresolved. Some moons are spiritually or magically inconsequential in practice—having no detectable effect at all—while a few may exert extraordinarily powerful influences. Lived religion: Worship, prayers, offerings, rites, pilgrimages, taboos and folk beliefs are widespread around most moons in at least some cultures, but not universal to every moon or every person. Different kingdoms and peoples may revere the same moon differently, reject one cult's interpretation, honor multiple moons or practice unrelated religious traditions. A celestial body, a magical influence, and a deity associated with that moon are not automatically identical. Do not force a single universally agreed pantheon. High-stakes possibility: A prayer to the 'right' moon could bring an astonishing boon, apparent miracle, transformation or intervention; an ill-chosen devotion could attract an ominous, malevolent or dark god's attention, with potentially terrible consequences. Prayers do not automatically work, and merely seeing a moon does not prove the worshipper knows which power, if any, answers. Blessings, bargains, curses, deceptions, local myths, coincidental successes and genuine divine interventions should be differentiated by actual evidence in the story; there is no fixed reward/curse table. Gods of magic genuinely exist as controlling magical powers; what remains unresolved is the identity and role of individual gods, their moon associations, and any particular dark deity's motives. Keep room for conflicting religious testimony, sincere belief, manipulation, false cults and tangible supernatural encounters, without forcing a single outcome. Campaign safeguard: No new moon, deity or lunar patron is named; no prayer, boon, curse, pact, revelation, doctrinal truth or character choice is inserted into Gloin's current campaign. The world-design material remains creator-revisable; the Era of Crowns, Fifth Age, Year 3847, Autumn Day 22 \~11:25 AM pause is unchanged. ## Moon-system scale retcon — 8.5× (creator decision, 21 November 2026) New current lunar population scale: Increase the present-day natural-satellite count by 8.5-fold over the earlier provisional 26–30 moons. These are worldbuilding changes, not discoveries or elapsed time in Gloin's campaign. ## First Age — one continuous Age, no eras; unknown length and reputed prosperity (creator decision, 21 November 2026) Creator canon: The First Age was one undivided Age, with no eras whatsoever. No formal, local, kingdom-specific, regional or historical era subdivisions are established within it; when constructing the official historical framework, do not invent a First Age era chronology. Its duration is entirely unknown, although later peoples and scholars guess it lasted thousands and thousands of years. Its characterization as a grand Age of Prosperity is later tradition and belief, not a historically verified description. Unbreakable source limitation: No records survive from before the first Great Cataclysm; therefore no surviving first-hand chronicles, inscriptional testimony, celestial logs, magical recordings or documented calendrical conversions prove First Age chronology, rulers, origins or level of prosperity. Do not invent a precise length, specific First Age civilization or definite name for its people as fact. The first Great Cataclysm ended the First Age and began the Second Age. Exactly which moons were involved and the catastrophe's causes remain open. Separate Second Age rule: The Second Age lasted exactly 1,437 years. No authenticated written histories, inscriptions, books, archives, celestial logs, eyewitness testimonies, preserved magical recordings or other verifiable contemporaneous records from the pre-Cataclysm First Age have survived into the known world. Never invent or let a current historian discover a surviving first-Age chronicle or first-hand recording as an ordinary source, and never treat a pre-Cataclysm date, monarch, civilization, religion, magic system or technological level as documentarily established. Canon safeguarding: The first lunar collision's exact moons, cause, chronological date, physical changes, all earlier civilizations and how life existed before the catastrophe remain unknown. Gloin's ancestry remains entirely undetermined and cannot be inferred through this gap. No in-story time advances. ## First Age ending — the original lunar Great Cataclysm (creator decision, 21 November 2026) Established high-level historical event: The very first great collision among Eryndor's moons in the ancient lunar history is the Great Cataclysm. Its worldwide consequences mark the end of the First Age and the beginning of the Second Age. This refers to the initial catastrophic moon collision, not any of the later lunar collisions or close-approach incidents that also occurred in deep antiquity. The first impact destroyed or shattered lunar bodies, contributed to the vast planetary debris rings, and profoundly changed the magical environment of the planet. The lunar system's later collisions, fragments and magical consequences remain possible separate events, not automatically ends of their own Ages. Preserved open history: The absolute date and duration of the First Age, identities and exact orbits of the original colliding moons, number of casualties, continent conditions, civilizations present, and complete causal sequence are not established. Do not force the First Throne, all ruins, or Gloin's ancestry to be connected to this cataclysm. The Third, Fourth and Fifth Age transitions remain unwritten. This ancient event does not progress present-day campaign time. The present date remains Autumn Day 22, Year 3847 of the Era of Crowns, Fifth Age. ## Era of Awakening — THREE simultaneous lunar-magical consequences, definitive correction (21 November 2026) Latest binding creator correction: The 321-year Era of Awakening at the start of Eryndor's 1,437-year Second Age was defined by all three, equally essential, transformations following the First Great Cataclysm: 1. PERMANENT LOSS: Before the Great Cataclysm, Eryndor had vastly more moons than the modern surviving roughly 221–255; the exact original count is unknown. When original moons were destroyed and their particular magical sources ceased to exist, entire associated forms of lunar magic were truly and irreversibly lost to Eryndor. These are not merely forgotten spells, temporarily weakened techniques, or powers awaiting rediscovery. Only First Age peoples could ever have witnessed or used certain such lost powers. No First Age records survive, so modern people cannot establish a reliable exhaustive roster or reconstruct those disappeared disciplines from intact original accounts. 2. BIRTH OF NEW MAGIC: Some fragments of shattered moons settled into new separate orbiting bodies — new “moons” — and became new sources of lunar magic with powers or disciplines not present before. The Cataclysm thus irreversibly reshaped the roster of lunar magics in both directions; it was simultaneously a destruction and a creation. The exact new-moon tally, identities, paths of formation, and individual disciplines remain unspecified. Other debris contributed to Eryndor's existing planetary rings; not every fragment becomes a magically potent moon. 3. UNRELIABILITY AND UPHEAVAL: In addition to those permanent changes, lunar magic was profoundly unstable and unreliable in the post-Cataclysm upheaval: some surviving powers fluctuated, faltered, became dangerous or unpredictable, and the newly arising lunar sources were poorly understood. Inconsistency and risk were a central reason many peoples learned that even powerful working magic could not be the only reliable foundation of agriculture, healing, infrastructure, water, food, defense, or daily survival. This does not force every existing power to fail everywhere at once or mean that all magic remains equally unstable forever. Different peoples' responses include nonmagical resilience, engineering, new magical inquiry and adaptations of existing traditions. Critical continuity: All three consequences matter, rather than replacing unreliability with lost/new magic or reducing permanently destroyed disciplines to temporarily unstable magic. The planet's independent Natural Magic / World's Breath remains extant; culturally distinct magical arts of Khazari, Eldar, Aelwyn, Gnomes, Pixies, etc. remain where they can function without annihilated lunar sources. The first Age lasted an unknown time, had no internal eras, and has no surviving records; it is only believed by later peoples to have been an exceptionally long age of prosperity. The specific count of moons destroyed, when and how fragments became stable new moons, and detailed lunar-magic mechanics are open. The moon-shattering, loss/birth of distinct powers, and instability are established as historical realities, even though surviving post-Cataclysm scholars may never have complete proof of every pre-Cataclysm discipline. Modern planetscape has roughly 221–255 moons (midpoint \~238), not an exact confirmed count. The Second Age's second era is the 1,000-year Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321); the Era of Fire lasted 116 years (Years 1,322–1,437). Do not retroactively connect the first throne mystery, Gloin's ancestry or any unapproved political narrative to the Cataclysm. ## Meaning of the Era of Awakening — lunar magical upheaval and the end of unquestioning reliance (creator direction, 21 November 2026) Creator-established central historical meaning: The Era of Awakening is named for the surviving peoples' realization, following the first Great Cataclysm, that magic was not an infallible foundation on which to rely for every necessity of life or government. The lunar collisions and destruction of magical source-moons caused an extraordinary upheaval in lunar magic, with lost or disrupted influences, unfamiliar changes, fluctuating effectiveness, unpredictable consequences and dangerous episodes. The exact magical physics of each disrupted source, spell or moon remain unknown; this does not assert that all disciplines failed simultaneously or that every place experienced the same severity. The awakening was philosophical and practical, not the initial discovery of magical powers: Post-Cataclysm peoples had to learn that if magic weakened, misbehaved or became unavailable for a particular task, ordinary material knowledge and workable contingencies still mattered. Reliably supplied food, water, shelter, medicine, roads, sanitation, mechanical systems, agriculture, trade, craftsmanship, engineering, recordkeeping and nonmagical fortifications could not be casually neglected. The cultural response varied across civilizations; magical research, religious reassessment, practical crafts, rebuilding and resilience could proceed together, often unevenly and through conflict. This is the conceptual reason for the 321-year first era of the 1,437-year Second Age (Second Age years 1–321). The era is not prescribed to have been universally peaceful or wholly technological. Important existing magic safeguard: Lunar moons are actual sources of lunar magic. Eryndor's Natural Magic / World's Breath has a separate planetary source and did not vanish as a mere consequence of damage to the moons. Do not retcon all magic into an extinguished lunar phenomenon, turn the world's peoples into non-magical societies, nullify established Khazari, Eldar, Aelwyn, Gnome, Pixie, and other culturally distinct traditions, or decree that an entire civilization permanently renounced magic. Instead the foundational lesson is that powerful magic can fail, change, corrupt or become unstable and civilizations should not be wholly dependent on its reliability. Some regions and arts might become less reliable while others remain workable or intensify; exact distribution is open. No surviving pre-Cataclysm records: The First Age is undocumented and its alleged long prosperity is an unverified later tradition. This historical awakening may be inferred from Second Age and later sources; it does not prove the precise magical infrastructure, technology, level of societal reliance or nature of any First Age civilization. Examples such as broken enchanted waterworks, failed magical defenses or disrupted healing are illustrative event ideas, not yet established incidents. Specific catastrophes, casualty totals, temples, wars, names of inventors, discoveries, moon identities, dates within the 321 years, and the event ending the Era of Awakening remain to be decided. Chronology and continuity: The First Age had no eras.
